verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Smithery can publish an MCP server you have already deployed elsewhere (via its URL), distribute local stdio bundles, and expose a locally running server via Uplink. Nothing shows it converting an OpenAPI definition or custom code into a hosted MCP server. The 'no protocol plumbing' claim (smithery-docs-1) is about consumers connecting to servers, which is a different story, and the hosted services were shut down on 2026-10-31.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn an existing API definition (OpenAPI) or custom code into a hosted MCP server without writing protocol plumbing
